issues.failure_explanation: The displayed sesquilinear form omits the k^{-2} factor in the highest-order term, so it is not the form associated with the CAP PDE in Definition def:CAP. Consequently it cannot be written as (u,v)_{H^1_k}+(μ u,v)_{L^2} with bounded μ, and the Gårding inequality eq:Garding used throughout is not valid for the form as written. The correct form is k^{-2}∫ A∇u·̸∇v − ∫(c^{-2}+iV)u̸v; the stated μ = −c_scat^2 − iV − 1 should also be −c_scat^{-2} − iV − 1.

failure_location.quote: a(u,v):=\int_\Omega (A_{\rm scat}\nabla u)\cdot\overline{\nabla v} - \big((c_{\rm scat})^{-2}+ \ri V\big) u\,\overline{v} \quad \tfor u,v \in H^1_0(\Omega).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor k^{-2} in the first term of eq:sesqui_CAP and change the expression for μ to −c_scat^{-2} − iV − 1.
issues.overall_effect: All results that use the sesquilinear form a (thm:main, cor:1, cor:2, cor:3, thm:final1, thm:final2) are unsupported as written; the Galerkin matrix and preconditioner are those of a different operator.
issues.title: CAP sesquilinear form missing k^{-2} factor
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced local factor; every substantive claim and guarantee is preserved after the insertion, so no new argument or loss of regime is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We highlight that the assumption that $\cT^h$ is quasi-uniform with simplicial elements means that [Assumption 5.2]{MeSa:10} holds with all the maps $R_K$ equal to the identity
We now use the bound on $\eta$ in Corollary \ref{cor:MS1} with $p_c=p_f$ and $h$ replaced by $H$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof applies Corollary cor:MS1 to the coarse space, but cor:MS1 (and its proof) require the mesh to be quasi-uniform. The hypotheses of thm:final1 only say that each coarse element is a union of fine elements; this does not imply that cT_H is quasi-uniform, since coarse elements can have widely varying diameters. Thus the bound on η(coarse) is used outside its hypotheses. The same gap occurs in thm:final2, where the coarse mesh is not assumed shape-regular but interpolation and approximation results are applied to it.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that the assumptions in \S\ref{sec:ass_fine} hold, and, additionally, $\coarse$ consists of piecewise polynomials on a simplicial mesh $\cT_H$, with diameter $H$, such that each element of $\cT_H$ is the union of a set of elements of $\cT_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the hypotheses that cT_H is quasi-uniform (for thm:final1) or shape-regular (for thm:final2), which is the standard local condition needed for the cited approximation results.
issues.overall_effect: The bounds on η(coarse) and hence the verification of Assumption ass:coarse and the conclusions of thm:final1 (and thm:final2) are not justified for non-quasi-uniform (respectively non-shape-regular) coarse meshes.
issues.title: Missing regularity hypothesis on the coarse mesh in thm:final1
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing regularity hypothesis is a short local condition; the advertised regimes and all rates survive unchanged.

Taking the Euclidean adjoint of B_L^{-1}(A^\dagger) gives first term R_0^T (A_0^\dagger)^{-1} R_0 (not R_0^T A_0^{-1} R_0) and middle sum Σ R_l^T (A_l^\dagger)^{-1} R_l (not Σ R_l^T A_l^{-1} R_l), because the Galerkin matrices A_0 and A_l are not Hermitian. The displayed right preconditioner omits these adjoints.

issues.title: Right preconditioner definition is not the adjoint of the left preconditioner

This requires the standard Schatz/adjoint-approximability argument using the bound on η(fine) from Corollary cor:MS1 (with h in place of H); the proof omits it.
